problems.question:
In a survey of 90 students, 25 said a cat is their favourite pet.
The survey results are to be shown in a display that compares each type of pet as a part of the whole group.
Name a suitable display and find the angle that would represent cats in it.

lines.text: Favourite pet is categorical data and the question compares parts of a whole, so a pie chart suits it.

problems.question:
A school canteen sells 420 lunches in a week. Of these, 56 are salads.
The canteen manager wants to show how the lunches sold are shared between the different types of lunch.
Name a suitable display and find the angle that would represent salads in it.

lines.text: Type of lunch is categorical data and the manager wants to show shares of a whole, so a pie chart suits it.

problems.question:
Five students recorded the number of hours, $x$, they studied for a test and their score, $y$.
$(1, 2), \; (2, 4), \; (3, 5), \; (4, 4), \; (5, 5)$
Use the statistics mode on your calculator to find the correlation coefficient $r$, correct to four decimal places.

steps.title: Use the statistics mode on the calculator

lines.text: Enter the hours as the $x$ values and the scores as the $y$ values.

problems.question:
A scientist wants to find the mean length of the 800 trout in a lake. She catches 40 of the trout and measures them.
Identify the population and the sample, and write the sample as a percentage of the population.

steps.title: Identify the population and the sample

lines.text: Population: all 800 trout in the lake. Sample: the 40 trout caught and measured.

steps.title: Write the sample as a fraction of the population

problems.question:
The number of text messages sent by 11 students in one day is shown, in order.
$3, \; 5, \; 6, \; 8, \; 9, \; 12, \; 14, \; 15, \; 17, \; 20, \; 22$
Find $Q_1$, $Q_3$ and the interquartile range.

steps.title: Find the median and split the ranked values into halves

lines.text: There are 11 values, so the median is the 6th value, $12$.
The lower half is $3, 5, 6, 8, 9$ and the upper half is $14, 15, 17, 20, 22$, leaving the median out.

steps.title: Find Q1 as the median of the lower half

lines.text: The median of 5 values is the 3rd value.

steps.title: Find Q3 as the median of the upper half

lines.text: The median of 5 values is the 3rd value.

steps.title: Subtract to get the interquartile range
